facts.statement: The holotype of Piatnitzkysaurus, a subadult individual, was estimated to be around 4.3 meters long and 450 kilograms in mass.
facts.quote: Piatnitzkysaurus was a relatively lightly built medium-sized bipedal carnivore that was around 4.3 m long and around 450 kg in mass, though such estimates apply to the holotype, which is a subadult.

facts.statement: The ischium of Piatnitzkysaurus is 423 millimeters long.
facts.quote: Its ischium is 423 mm long.

facts.statement: The braincase of Piatnitzkysaurus features a parasphenoid recess, a trait found in only two other non-avian theropods, Sinovenator and Sinornithosaurus.
facts.quote: An unusual feature of the braincase is the parasphenoid recess, which has only been described in two other non-avian theropods, Sinovenator and Sinornithosaurus.

facts.statement: The braincase of Piatnitzkysaurus possesses a prominent hook-like basisphenoidal wing, a feature also seen in Ceratosaurus, Allosaurus, and Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Another noteworthy aspect of the braincase is the prominent hook-like basisphenoidal wing, a feature that is also found in other theropods such as Ceratosaurus, Allosaurus, and Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Piatnitzkysaurus was collected during expeditions in 1977, 1982, and 1983 from the Cañadón Asfalto Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Piatnitzkysaurus, PVL 4073, was collected during expeditions in 1977, 1982, and 1983 at the Cañadón Asfalto Formation

facts.statement: The type species Piatnitzkysaurus floresi was described by Jose Bonaparte in 1979.
facts.quote: The type species, Piatnitzkysaurus floresi, was described by Jose Bonaparte in 1979.

facts.statement: The genus name Piatnitzkysaurus was named to honor Alejandro Matveievich Piatnitzky, a Russian-born Argentine geologist.
facts.quote: It was named to honor Alejandro Matveievich Piatnitzky (1879–1959), a Russian-born Argentine geologist.

facts.statement: Piatnitzkysaurus is part of the most basal clade within Megalosauroidea, which also contains Condorraptor, Marshosaurus, and Xuanhanosaurus.
facts.quote: The most basal clade within Megalosauroidea contains Condorraptor, Marshosaurus, Piatnitzkysaurus and Xuanhanosaurus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Condorraptor is a distinct species or merely individual variation within Piatnitzkysaurus due to their strong resemblance.
facts.quote: Due to the strong resemblance to Piatnitzkysaurus, it has been suggested that the sister taxa Condorraptor could be better interpreted as the result of individual variation within the species, and not as separate taxa.

facts.statement: Piatnitzkysaurus is classified in the family Piatnitzkysauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Piatnitzkysauridae

facts.statement: Piatnitzkysaurus floresi is the only known species in the genus Piatnitzkysaurus, a megalosauroid theropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Piatnitzkysaurus floresi (lagarto de Piatnitzky) es la única especie conocida del género Piatnitzkysaurus, un dinosaurio terópodo megalosauroideo

facts.statement: Piatnitzkysaurus was a medium-sized theropod with a light build and robust arms, measuring between 4 and 5 meters long and weighing up to 275 kilograms.
facts.quote: Piatnitzkysaurus era un terópodo mediano, de ligera constitución y robustos brazos, midiendo entre 4 y 5 metros de largo y llegando a pesar 275 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Fully developed adults of Piatnitzkysaurus are estimated to have reached a length of 6.6 meters.
facts.quote: Se ha estimado que un adulto completamente desarrollado llegaría a crecer hasta 6,6 metros de largo.

facts.statement: The skull of Piatnitzkysaurus was 50 centimeters long and lightened by large fenestrae.
facts.quote: El cráneo tenía 50 centímetros de longitud y estaba aligerado por grandes fenestras.

facts.statement: Piatnitzkysaurus possessed conical, highly compressed, long, backward-curving, and sharp teeth.
facts.quote: Estaba armado con dientes cónicos muy comprimidos, largos, curvados hacia atrás y afilados.

facts.statement: Piatnitzkysaurus had robust arms and powerful hind legs with four toes on each foot.
facts.quote: Tenía brazos robustos y poderosas patas traseras con cuatro dedos en cada pie.

facts.statement: The ischium of Piatnitzkysaurus measures 423 millimeters in length.
facts.quote: Su isquion mide 423 milímetros de largo.

facts.statement: In contrast to its hind legs, the front legs of Piatnitzkysaurus were very small and ended in three clawed digits.
facts.quote: Las patas delanteras, en contraste, eran muy pequeñas y tenían tres dedos terminados en garras.

facts.statement: The type species Piatnitzkysaurus floresi was described by José Fernando Bonaparte in 1979.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, P. floresi, fue descrita por José Fernando Bonaparte en 1979.

facts.statement: The species was named in honor of Alejandro Matveievich Piatnitzky (1879–1959), an Argentine geologist born in Russia.
facts.quote: La especie fue nombrada en honor a Alejandro Matveievich Piatnitzky (1879-1959), un geólogo argentino nacido en Rusia.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database records the time range of Piatnitzkysaurus as the Toarcian, from 182.9 to 180.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (182.9 to 180.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: Its light build would have conferred great speed on Piatnitzkysaurus.
facts.quote: Su diseño ligero le habría conferido gran velocidad.

facts.statement: When holding its prey with its jaws, Piatnitzkysaurus's claws would wound the flesh, causing bleeding until the prey was too weak to resist.
facts.quote: Cuando sujetaba a su víctima con sus mandíbulas, las garras lastimaban la carne haciéndola sangrar hasta que la presa estaba demasiado débil para seguir resistiéndose.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the affiliation of Piatnitzkysauridae with Megalosauroidea is supported, as future analyses might classify them outside Megalosauroidea.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la afiliación de estos clados con Megalosauroidea no está respaldada por las métricas de soporte de árboles, y es posible que se clasifiquen fuera de Megalosauroidea en análisis futuros.

facts.statement: Piatnitzkysaurus is the only member of Piatnitzkysauridae with preserved cranial material, including two maxillae, a frontal, a skull, and a partial dentary.
facts.quote: Piatnitzkysaurus es el único miembro de Piatnitzkysauridae con material craneal conservado, del que se conocen dos maxilares, un frontal, un cráneo y un dentario parcial.
